findings.where: Style tile, the five section labels (desktop-02, desktop-03, phone-01 to phone-03): 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline rule under the label, but 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'A blog post page' have none
findings.fault: The labels are the same kind of part, set in the same small semibold sans, but only two of the five have a rule under them. The tile is meant to set the house style, and it treats the same heading two ways with no reason given. On the phone, where the sections stack, the rule appears and disappears from one section to the next.
findings.who_objects: The designer of the layout round (#8 round 2), who has to draw inside this tile. They cannot tell whether a section heading takes a rule or not, so whichever way they choose, half the tile goes against it.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the principle words 'calm, precise, light' (desktop-03, phone-02)
findings.fault: This is the sketch's display line, but it is set in large semibold Source Sans in the lighter grey. The tile's own type pair says Gelasio is for display and Source Sans for 'the nav, buttons, labels and dates only'. Every other display line on the page is Gelasio in logo grey: the hero headline, 'Gelasio', and the post title. This one line breaks the type rule the tile has just stated.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, who are judging whether the site and the logo 'speak in one voice'. They see the tile contradict its own type pairing at the one place that names the motion's character.

findings.where: Apostrophes: the hero standfirst ('World Bank's'), the blog post title ('The World's Best…'), and the type-pair note ('Georgia's', 'logo's'), on desktop and phone
findings.fault: These apostrophes are straight typewriter marks. The same page uses curly quotes elsewhere: the post's “…” quotes and the related link's ‘Abundance’. At headline size in Gelasio, the straight mark in 'World's' stands out, and it sits right next to correctly set curly marks.
findings.who_objects: Mark, a lawyer whose name and careful drafting are the brand, and a development-bank reader of his posts. Mixed straight and curly marks in a title look like copy pasted from a plain-text file, not a typeset page, and that undercuts the 'experience and judgement' the page is selling.

findings.where: Hero, the Mist panel holding the portrait stand-in against the white page (desktop-01, phone-01); the 'Mist #F3F6F9' swatch in the palette
findings.fault: Mist is about ΔE00 2.6 from the white ground and shares a long edge with it. That is below the house's line of 3 for two large near-white greys that touch, so it reads as a near-miss, not as a chosen surface. The panel looks like an off-white rendering fault, and on a poor or bright screen it vanishes. It is also the only fill on a direction whose card says 'nothing in a panel'.
findings.who_objects: The founder and Mark, who are judging the v5 'true white' direction from this screen. The right third of the first screen looks like a slightly dirty white, not either white or a deliberate tone.
